thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: p99 latency spike detected across streaming endpoints (routes: /v1/stream, /v1/chat/stream). Service: prefix-cache. Start: 2026-03-15T09:02:08Z. Automated triage: increased cache miss rate on new salt namespace (kv-salt v7).

maria: I’m on it. Saw p95 jump from ~120ms to ~850ms and p99s hitting ~3.6s. Streaming stalls (clients waiting on first token) correlate with high prefix missrate.

sam: @maria can you confirm if this is a rollout? I saw a salt rotation job went out ~09:00 UTC by infra-deploy.

alex: yep, deploy pipeline shows `kv-salt:update -> v7` rolled to canary at 08:58 and to prod at 08:59. There was a config flip: `prefix_hash_salt = "s7-2026-03"`.

maria: logs show a surge in `cache_lookup_miss` with keys that look like old-salt and new-salt mix. Likely compatibility/rehash edge between instances.

emily: Customer impact: some enterprise customers (acct: ACME-Cloud) reported real-time stream pauses and reconnects. Support ticket #4231 opened. Support bot attached traces.

support-bot: Ticket #4231: "We saw users drop during streaming responses around 09:03 UTC, multiple reconnects." Attached trace ids: trace-9876, trace-9877.

ryan: Oncall handoff note: I’m taking lead for mitigation. Priorities: 1) stop customer impact 2) restore cache hitrate 3) root cause.

sam: Quick mitigation idea: pin routing to pre-rotation prefix-salt for read-paths (force old salt variant) and stop further rotations. Can we stop the rollout and roll back the salt config?

alex: We can flip a feature flag in the routing layer to prefer `kv-salt v6` for 10m. Command:

```
POST /admin/feature-flags/prefix_salt_prefer
{ "value": "v6", "ttl": 600 }
```

maria: Doing the flag flip now.

maria: :white_check_mark: Flag applied. Observability: cache-miss rate dropping on the routing slice that got the change.

sam: Can you paste current metrics? I’m watching p95/p99.

maria: p95 down to ~180ms, p99 down to ~800ms. Still above baseline but trending.

ryan: Good. Next: we need a coordinated rollback of the salt rollout and a plan to rehash keys without causing SLO spikes. @alex can infra roll back the salt user config? What’s the fastest safe path?

alex: Rollback path: revert config to v6 and requeue offending nodes for cache warmup. Risk: transient extra CPU due to prefetch. Timeline ~12-18m to fully warm.

kevin: Suggestion: enable short-term aggressive prefix warmup on a small subset of hot shards to reduce storming. Script to raise prefetch factor:

```
for shard in hot_shards:
  POST /shard/$shard/prefetch?factor=4
```

maria: starting warmup scripts for top 20 shards.

emily: Noted: ACME reported 12k affected requests at peak, TTLs expired roughly in same window. We should notify their CSM and log the incident.

support-bot: Notifying CSMs for affected enterprise customers: sent.

sam: We should create an incident postmortem checklist: what caused salt flip to go to prod without staged compatibility test? Who approved pipeline? Need action items.

ryan: Agreed — after stabilization. For now, keep the feature flag pinned and start rollback. Also open a canary watch to ensure we don’t get a second drift.

alex: Rollback started at 09:12 UTC. Prod config reverted. Prefetch jobs running. I’ll post when all nodes report `salt=v6`.

maria: Observability: steady decrease in cache-miss from 42% -> 8% over 6 minutes post-rollback. P99 now ~210ms. Streaming stalls trending to baseline.

sam: Good work. We will delay any further salt rotations until we have a migration plan. Create a follow-up doc for migration strategy (rehash backfill, compatibility layer, canary sizes).

ryan: Oncall handoff: I’ll stay for 30 more minutes then hand to @sam for overnight. Please include a short summary in the handoff message.

maria: Summary for handoff: "prefix-salt v7 rollout caused mixed-key missstorm; mitigated by pinning v6 via feature flag and rolling back config; prefetch warmed hot shards; p99 reduced to ~210ms; customer ACME impacted, support notified. Next: postmortem + safe migration plan."

sam: I’ll pick up. If anything flares, ping `#eng-oncall` and call with :phone:.

emily: I’m drafting customer-facing notes for ACME and wider status update for status.redwood.ai.

support-bot: Incident timeline recorded to OpsLog ID: ops-5199998888.

ryan: Thanks everyone. Marking incident as mitigated for now but leaving P1 open until postmortem created and rollback verified across all regions.

maria: logging artifacts: heap of traces under /var/logs/prefix-cache/2026-03-15/5199998888/*.gz and prefetch job output uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-ops/prefetch/5199998888/

sam: Action items created: [A1] Postmortem (owner: alex), [A2] Add migration compatibility tests to CI (owner: kevin), [A3] Improve canary gating (owner: maria). I'll create cards.

kevin: Also recommend a small integration test that simulates salt flip and verifies hitrate with mixed clients.

maria: OK closing live thread for coordination. Leaving it open for postmortem threads. :thumbsup:
